no-mistakes(ci): Fixed the cause of the WebSocket upgrade 403 on 279cd36a41. The fault is in the scale test harness, not in authentication. The changes are left uncommitted in the worktree. **Root cause** - The private artifact was read through a filter that dropped any line mentioning cookies, tokens, CSRF or credentials. - It shows 336 "Failed to read token revocation" warnings and 344 DBConnection "connection not available and request was dropped from queue after ~2000-2750ms" errors, in bursts of 84 between 22:13:12 and 22:13:23. - It also shows 8 BitmapIndex tasks that could not check out a connection. - The cause: each replica peer inherited the test config's `pool: Ecto.Adapters.SQL.Sandbox`, and `Replica.start` set Sandbox `:auto` mode. - In `:auto` mode, any process that queries owns its connection until it exits. Each WebSocket handler process reads token revocation, the user and permissions on connect, then stays alive, so it kept its connection. - About 8 sockets per replica (`TEST_CNPG_POOL_SIZE=8`; run-scoped peak 24 = 8 + 2x8) took the whole pool. The other upgrades waited in the queue, were dropped, `UserSocket.connect` returned `:error`, and Phoenix answered 403. - Session, CSRF and cookie construction were all correct: the 16 sockets that got a connection upgraded fine. **Invariant:** a long-lived request process in a replica must never hold a database connection between queries. Every place this must hold is a replica Repo checkout: socket connect, channel and HTTP handlers, and the BitmapIndex and WorldCache tasks. All of them share one boundary, the replica's Repo pool, and the fix is made there. **Fix** - `replica.exs` starts Repo with the production `DBConnection.ConnectionPool`. Pool size and queue limits are still inherited unchanged. - The `Sandbox.mode(Repo, :auto)` call is removed. - Unchanged: CSRF, cookie session, Guardian and revocation checks, RBAC (`analytics.view` plus `devices.view`, viewer role), filtering, workload, deadlines, and every pool, time, memory, admission and cleanup limit. No heartbeats were added. **Preflight** (in `topology_bitmap_scale_acceptance_test.exs`) - Right after the peers start, and before the 600-second publisher wait, `Client.upgrades/2` opens 50 concurrent authenticated upgrades per server and holds them open. The test requires `%{upgraded: 50}`. - This exercises the same session, CSRF, token and RBAC boundary as the viewers, and it fails on a pinned pool. It catches this failure without spending the geometry and viewer phases, though the 1.1M seed still runs first. **Diagnostics** - The Client now stops with `{:upgrade_refused, status}`. - Its `format_status/1` redacts the session (cookie and CSRF token) from crash reports. - A new harness regression drives a real Client against a loopback server that answers 403. It asserts the stop reason and that neither synthetic secret appears in the captured log. - Negative control: the pre-fix client fails it with `unexpected_transport` (invocation a961890e-89cd-4e21-abe2-dd4c3836f37f). **Docs:** `docs/topology-bitmap-scale-acceptance.md` now describes the production pool, why the Sandbox is not used, and the preflight. It claims no scale pass. **Verification (`--config=remote`)** - `//elixir/web-ng:format`: already formatted. - `//elixir/web-ng:topology_bitmap_scale_harness_test` and `//elixir/web-ng:quality_check`: both passed (cd1e52a1-bc8f-4437-b0e0-8d18f6458b39). - Full `make test`: 419 passed, 2 Swift tests skipped (a479d757-6921-44fa-85d8-52908ff97e47). - `git diff --check`: clean. **Not run:** the hosted compact and sparse `topology_bitmap_scale_*_acceptance` runs, which need the shared fixture. The pool fix and the upgrade preflight have not executed against a real database yet, and scale acceptance (task 4.2) stays open. No hosted dispatch, publication or no-mistakes config change was made, and no credential, cookie, header or rc content was printed. The temporary filter files were deleted

no-mistakes(ci): I changed only elixir/web-ng/test/phoenix/topology/bitmap_queries_db_test.exs. The test has not run yet: it only runs in the in-cluster PR CI lane topology_atlas_db_test_0, so the run on the republished head will be its first. Cause (rule: a held watch result must be judged only by the delivery-time check): TopologyTileChannel schedules a refresh tick 5-10 s after join and then every 5 s (topology_tile_channel.ex:25 and :84). Refresh re-checks authorization and closes the channel with topology_error when access is revoked. All three held-watch cases (expired, remapped, revoked) ran on one long-lived channel. A tick that fired while the channel was suspended sat in its mailbox ahead of the finished result. In revoked_ref it ran first and closed the channel, so the expected forbidden reply never arrived, which matches the CI mailbox. The same reordering could affect the other two cases. The held window also contained :deactivate, which runs RevokeUserAccess and audit/JetStream work synchronously. That widened the window for a tick and could also spend the one-second deadline. Fix (all three held cases): - A new helper rejoin/2 leaves the current channel and joins a new real channel right before each held watch. A new channel's first tick is at least 5 s away, and each held window ends within 1 s of its watch starting (the expiry case deliberately waits 1.1 s), so a tick cannot get ahead of the result. - I removed the assert_push of the old channel's _replaced_reset frame before the expiry case. That frame only appeared because the old channel still held an earlier view; a fresh channel has none, so it no longer happens. It was setup noise, not a delivery check. - The revoked case now sets the user's status to inactive with a direct Repo.update_all that must change exactly one row. That is the same field CurrentUserAuthority reads. The real :deactivate action stays covered by the owner test at line 302, with its forbidden and HTTP 403 results unchanged. Unchanged: production deadlines, fences, all application code, and the exact assertions for source_changed, the deliberate 1.1 s query_timeout, forbidden at delivery, no frame pushed for each refused case, the overlay HTTP 403, and the explicit :tile_tick check that pushes topology_error forbidden and closes the channel with :normal. No sleeps, retries or loosened matches were added. Verification: bazel test --config=remote //elixir/web-ng:quality_check (format and Credo) passed on RBE: https://carverauto.buildbuddy.io/invocation/b5e88770-e9f7-4985-88f2-8577be41f213. Nothing has compiled this file yet; compiling and running it are left to the CI lane. I relied on Phoenix's standard leave/1 behaviour from memory because the Phoenix source is not available locally

no-mistakes(ci): Test-only fixes for all 5 failures in hosted topology_atlas_db_test child 74651345; no production code changed. (1) bitmap_queries_db_test :300 failed with unknown registry ServiceRadarWebNG.PubSub: the DB lane doesn't start the app, so the endpoint's PubSub server was missing. Setup now starts it under supervision next to ServiceRadar.PubSub. The :548 test needed it too because it also joins the channel. (2) :548 catalog_not_ready: ServiceRadar.PrefixTags.Registry wasn't running, so BitmapPrefixTags.sources/0 returned :prefix_registry_unavailable and the real BitmapIndex owner never scheduled catalog preparation. The test now starts the real registry only when none is running, and reuses one the app already owns. No manual catalog shortcut; cold-start, expiry and failure-reset checks unchanged. (3) bitmap_replica_lifecycle_db_test :70: BitmapSource.dictionary_page uses Ash.Query.timeout(5_000), and Ash runs reads with a timeout in a child task. The observer only counted queries from direct children of the loader supervisor, so it saw head and progress queries but never page queries, matching the mailbox. The observer now credits each query to the loader turn among self() and $callers, and held pages are released on the actually blocked process (release_page/2). This also makes the existing refute :page checks meaningful. Reuse, 60s throttle, 180s budget, geometry and late-commit assertions unchanged. (4,5) :262 and :501, Postgrex 25001: PostgreSQL rejects SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL in a savepoint only when the level changes. The boxed sandbox ran the test's query and the publisher transaction as savepoints at the default level. The boxed cases now open their shared sandbox owner at REPEATABLE READ (the sibling test's approach), so the publisher's statement is a no-op and its isolation contract holds. They keep rollback-only isolation, the tag-derived ownership timeout and TestSupport.stop_repo_owner teardown; unboxed cases still use checkout_repo!. no-mistakes(ci): Fixed the single failing BazelCI target: //elixir/serviceradar_core:unit_tests_serviceradar_other. ROOT CAUSE. The CI run reported "259 tests pass, 1 fails remotely" — one target, failing on a wall-clock assertion. Across its two attempts, TWO DIFFERENT tests failed the SAME assertion `assert usec < 250_000`: attempt 1 at otel_logs_exporter_test.exs:155 ("prepare drops extra events...", left 286406) and attempt 2 at :139 ("prepare converts charlist bodies...", left 320535). A different test each attempt is the signature of executor contention, not a regression — the suite is `async: true` with 867 tests on a shared/contended RBE executor, so a 250ms budget measures machine load, not the code. The assertion was introduced by THIS PR in commit 56cdf2fc52, so it is this change's defect to fix. FIX (1 file, +8/-12, elixir/serviceradar_core/test/serviceradar/telemetry/otel_logs_exporter_test.exs). Removed the three `:timer.tc` / `usec < 250_000` machine-speed proxies and kept the deterministic bounds they stood in for — those already encode the actual regression the otel commits fixed (bodies truncated to <=8KiB via `byte_size(body) <= 8_192 + ...`; batch trimmed via `length(prepared.undefined) == 256`; huge report replaced via `payload == "<truncated>"`). Where the timer was the only thing left guarding the `to_proto` call, replaced it with a deterministic assertion that the bound reaches the ENCODER OUTPUT rather than just the intermediate map: `assert %{resource_logs: [%{scope_logs: [%{log_records: records}]}]} = proto` plus `length(records) == 2` / `== 256`. Renamed "stays bounded and cheap" -> "stays bounded" since "cheap" is no longer claimed. No coverage lost: deleting the truncation or the 256-trim fails the deterministic assertions immediately. VERIFICATION. - Exact failing target on the same RBE pool: PASSED in 64.4s, then PASSED in 64.8s on a second --nocache_test_results run. - Load-bearing proof (assertions are not vacuous): mutating `== 2`->`3` and `== 256`->`255` makes the target FAILED in 2 out of 2 attempts; restored and re-confirmed green. - Full BazelCI-equivalent sweep: bazel test -c opt --config=remote --//build:enable_integration_tests //... --test_tag_filters=-integration_test,-acceptance_test,-benchmark -> exit 0, 260 pass / 0 fail / 2 skipped (CI's failing run was 259/1/2). - python3 -m unittest ci_heavy_gate_contract_test -> 56 tests OK; mix format --check-formatted -> clean. NOTES. The file is `not_selected` in INTEGRATION_SOURCE_DISPOSITIONS.tsv and its test count is unchanged at 5, so no disposition row or SERIAL_INTEGRATION_SELECTED_TEST_COUNTS update was needed (//build:integration_selection_equivalence_test and //:ci_heavy_gate_contract_test both pass). The only other `:timer.tc` in the suite (prefix_tags/benchmark_test.exs) is `@moduletag :benchmark`, excluded by CI's -benchmark filter; pre-existing and untouched. No product/source code changed — the defect was entirely in the test's verification method

no-mistakes(ci): I fixed this failure by changing the test's setup order; no product code changed. The new test sequence has not been run, because that suite only runs in the in-cluster PR CI. The re-run of `topology_atlas_db_test_0` on the republished head will be the first check of it. **Cause:** the channel sets a one-second deadline when a watch starts (`bitmap_stream.ex:96` and `:226`) and checks it again at delivery (`:162`). In the `remapped_ref` step, the test held a finished watch with the channel suspended and only then called `seal_mapping`. That helper does a FleetIdentity database lookup for each device and builds the replacement mapping natively, and all of that ran inside the held watch's one second. On a busy CI executor it ran past the deadline, so the delivery check returned `query_timeout` before it got to the source-change check. That explains why the test fails only sometimes and why the earlier revisions passed this suite: the a133 commit only changed two Rust test loops. **Fix:** in `elixir/web-ng/test/phoenix/topology/bitmap_queries_db_test.exs`, the test now seals the replacement mapping before `hold_completed_watch`. Only `WorldCache.install_ordinals` (installing the new mapping) and resuming the channel happen inside the held window. Sealing a mapping without installing it does not change which mapping the watch uses, so the source change still happens after the worker has finished. The test therefore still checks that delivery is refused with `source_changed`. **Checked the other steps:** the separate expiry step still waits 1.1 seconds on purpose and still expects `query_timeout`. The lint path (`scripts/elixir_quality.sh --lint-only`) exports SERVICERADAR_SKIP_NIF_COMPILATION=1, and Rustler skips cargo only when `Application.compile_env(:serviceradar_core, ServiceRadar.PrefixTags.Native, [])` returns `skip_compilation?: true`. That value comes from the TOP-LEVEL project's config (dependency configs are not evaluated by Mix), and `elixir/serviceradar_core_elx/config/config.exs` was missing the `ServiceRadar.PrefixTags.Native` entry that `serviceradar_core/config/config.exs` and `web-ng/config/config.exs` already had. Invariant: every top-level Mix project whose lint path compiles `serviceradar_core` as a path dependency must list every core Rustler NIF module (Dgraph, NetworkConfig, DispositionKernels, Zen, PrefixTags, TopologyAtlas) plus `serviceradar_srql`'s NIF in its SERVICERADAR_SKIP_NIF_COMPILATION skip block. Fix: added the missing `config :serviceradar_core, ServiceRadar.PrefixTags.Native, skip_compilation?: true` to `elixir/serviceradar_core_elx/config/config.exs`. Closed the sibling site too: `elixir/serviceradar_agent_gateway/config/config.exs` (also compiles core as a path dep, and is a matrix leg) was missing both `PrefixTags.Native` and `TopologyAtlas.Native`, so both were added with the same one-line pattern. The CI log itself proves the mechanism: every other NIF in the same block was already listed and was skipped during the failed run (compilation reached prefix_tags before the first cargo error), so the identical one-line addition resolves it. Root cause: migration 20261005130000_add_agent_supersession.exs contained `execute("UPDATE platform.ocsf_agents SET status = 'unavailable' WHERE status = 'superseded'")` in `down/0`, which trips the startup-safety grep for `UPDATE platform.` (it scans the whole file, including rollback). Its 2.9MB test.log (pulled via the BuildBuddy API) carries TWO independent PR-caused defects in the lane this PR joined: 1. `elixir/web-ng/test/phoenix/live/dashboard_live/netflow_map_geo_test.exs:96` — `seed_anchor!/5` bound a CIDR string to `$2::cidr`, so Postgres inferred the parameter as `cidr` and Postgrex raised `(DBConnection.EncodeError) expected %Postgrex.INET{}, got "192.0.2.0/24"`. Fix: `($2::text)::cidr` — verbatim the remedy this repo's `.agents/skills/srql-fixtures-db-tests/SKILL.md` documents under Common Failures. The new module adds 2 cases, so the `after_suite` gate failed separately: "executed 125 tests; expected exactly 123". Bumped to 125, the count the CI runner itself observed. `git log` confirms the helper was last touched pre-branch. **RustSec audit — fixed by upgrading, not suppressing.** RUSTSEC-2026-0286 (OOB read, cryptoki 0.12.0) reached only via `rust/rdp-connector-probe` → `ironrdp-connector =0.10.0` → `sspi 0.21.1`. Prior rounds proved it is not PR-caused and recommended either a documented `--ignore` or a bump to >=0.12.1. I took the bump: the workflow's two existing ignores are each justified as "no fixed upgrade is available", which is false here — `sspi` requires `cryptoki ^0.12`, so 0.12.1 is a plain patch bump. `cargo update -p cryptoki --precise 0.12.1` changed 2 lines of the detached probe lockfile; `bazel --batch mod deps --lockfile_mode=update` changed 1 line of MODULE.bazel.lock (the cryptoki fact). No `--ignore` added, no workflow edit. Verification, each with a command behind it: - Scratch DB on the srql-fixtures CNPG cluster per the skill; all branch migrations replayed on an empty database. Focused run of the new file: **2 tests, 0 failures**. - Fail-before proof: reverting the cast reproduced the CI failure verbatim (same error, stacktrace, line 133); restored after. - `cargo-audit` v0.22.2 (official tarball, run from /tmp, not installed) against a fresh advisory-db clone with the workflow's exact flags: RUSTSEC-2026-0286 gone. Baseline control on the pre-bump lockfile reproduced it. A `chacha20 0.10.1` yanked warning appears on BOTH lockfiles locally — pre-existing, and invisible in CI whose yanked lookup errors out for every crate (the wall of "No such crate in crates.io index" noise in the job log). - `bazel test -c opt --config=remote //rust/rdp-connector-probe:all` → 1/1 PASSED; `bazel query` shows `@rdp_connector_crates//:cryptoki-0.12.1`, so the hub really re-resolved. - Full CI test phase: `bazel test -c opt --config=remote --//build:enable_integration_tests //... --test_tag_filters=-integration_test,-acceptance_test,-benchmark` → **260 pass, 2 skipped, 0 failures** across 262 targets (invocation 2c0c0e56). - `//:all //build:all` → 12/12 pass, incl. `web_ng_db_runner_contract_test` and `ci_heavy_gate_contract_test`. `mix format --check-formatted` clean on both changed files. Deliberately reverted: `bazel run //third_party/crate_mirror:sync` wanted to fetch 85 archives and prune 21 — the mirror was already stale independent of this change, and its BUILD.bazel documents it as a `--distdir` fallback that "degrades to the old behaviour instead of breaking the build". Syncing would have added ~106 unrelated binary files; the now-unused cryptoki-0.12.0.crate simply degrades to a download, like the 84 crates already missing. no-mistakes(ci): I fixed all three defects behind the WebNgDbDiagnostic compact failure on f4bea662. The changes touch only the test harness and one doc, and are left uncommitted in the worktree. No production code, workload size, time, admission, pool, memory or cleanup limit changed. **1. HTTP 403 on tile receipts (root cause: missing role profiles)** - **Invariant:** every scale session's viewer must get its current authority from the real catalog's `viewer` role profile. - **Why it broke:** `CurrentUserAuthority` looks up the viewer's profile with `RoleProfile.get_by_system_name("viewer")`. A freshly provisioned clone has no built-in profiles. In production they are created at boot, and in the ordinary suites by `RoleProfileSeeder.seed()` in `test/test_helper.exs`. The scale target loads `test/db/topology_bitmap_scale_test_helper.exs` instead, which never seeds them. Before the round-7 reorder, `networks_live_db_test` ran first on serial_0 and its test_helper seeded them. With scale running first, the profile lookup returned nil, authorization was denied, and the tile request got 403. - **Fix:** the scale helper now runs the same production `RoleProfileSeeder.seed()`. It is idempotent, and compact and sparse share that helper. - **Precondition:** right after creating the user, the acceptance test asserts `RBAC.authorize_current(Scope.for_user(user), ["analytics.view", "devices.view"])`. A missing profile now fails at that point instead of as a later 403. - **Unchanged:** both permissions are still required, filtering stays always-on, and there is no admin role, bypass, or disabled-auth path. The seeded profiles are not deleted afterwards. They are boot baseline state, which test_helper.exs also leaves in place and reseeds. **2. Meter handler detaching** - **Invariant:** a query telemetry event can never detach the Meter, and a detached Meter can never pass scale. - **Correction to the evidence:** the failing increment `{3,nil}` is position 3, which is `rows`, not `query_time`. A transaction statement reports `num_rows: nil`. - **Fix in `Meter.query/4`:** - rows counts only an integer `num_rows`, otherwise 0; - each timing (`query_time`, `decode_time`, `queue_time`) uses `Map.get(timing, k) || 0`, so missing or nil values are handled. - **Missing evidence:** `Meter.report` now returns `instrumented`, which is true only while the handler is still attached. The acceptance test asserts it for both replicas, so stale counters left after a detach cannot pass. - **Regression test:** added to `topology_bitmap_scale_harness_test`. It sends an Ecto commit event (nil rows, nil `decode_time`) and a select through the real telemetry dispatch. It asserts the handler is still attached and the counts are `queries: 2, rows: 3`, then detaches the handler and asserts `instrumented` is false. - Pre-fix negative control (invocation 4691d53c-32c2-4d5d-8674-3863f9eb5eea): reproduced the hosted `Reason=:badarg` detach, and the test failed. **3. Dirty CPU schedulers** - ERTS caps dirty CPU schedulers at the normal scheduler count, so `+S 4:4 +SDcpu 8` actually gave 4, which matches the runtime `ds:4:4` report. - The peer now requests `+SDcpu 4`, which is the same resources. The acceptance test asserts both peers report 4 schedulers and 4 dirty CPU schedulers. - `docs/topology-bitmap-scale-acceptance.md` now says four dirty CPU schedulers and why. **Verification (`--config=remote`)** - `//elixir/web-ng:format`: already formatted. - `//elixir/web-ng:quality_check` and `:topology_bitmap_scale_harness_test`: both passed (939e4406-ca7e-4e97-b8bd-29449684204b). - Full `make test`: 419 passed, 2 skipped (331b91d1-a5c4-4bc0-84ea-f7ecb044ff9e). **Not run:** the hosted compact and sparse `topology_bitmap_scale_*_acceptance` runs. They need the hosted shared fixture, so the seeding fix and the authority precondition have not executed yet and need hosted WebNgDbDiagnostic on the new SHA. Scale acceptance remains pending. No hosted dispatch, publication or no-mistakes config change was made, and no credentials, cookies or headers were printed

no-mistakes(ci): Fixed BazelCI AlertEvaluationInboxTest 'a blocked owner neither delays another rule nor loses its input when killed' (expected {:ok,{:processed,:completed}}, got {:ok,:busy}). Invariant: Owner.advance returns :busy while any transaction holds the rule's transaction-scoped advisory fence (pg_try_advisory_xact_lock on Inbox.evaluation_key(rule_id)); it succeeds only after that transaction ends. Process.exit(blocked,:kill) delivers DOWN as soon as the Erlang process dies, but DBConnection reclaims the checkout and rolls back asynchronously, so the dead owner's fence can still be held when the next advance runs — a test-synchronization race, not a product defect (fence correctly reported busy). Test-only fix at the single affected site: after kill/locker release, wait_until(fence_free?(rule.id)) probes the exact production try-lock expression in a throwaway transaction (lock releases on commit, consumes no work) before the single unchanged Owner.advance assertion. No weakened assertion, skip, timeout inflation, retry of the assertion, or production change. Verified: git diff --check clean, //elixir/serviceradar_core:format already formatted, //elixir/serviceradar_core:quality_check PASSED (RBE 35.5s), all 4 integration_selection_load_only runners PASSED (edited file compiles/loads). no-mistakes(ci): Root-caused both checks via BuildBuddy invocation logs (bb view), since the harness's log retrieval was unavailable. SrqlParity: genuine regression from this PR. `metrics.edge.upper_bound` (timeseries_metrics, bucket:1h, agg:sum) disagreed — CNPG=1 row, StarRocks=2 rows (extra row exactly at the hour boundary, value 100.0). StarRocks's dialect always widens a whole-hour-multiple bucket query to the full hour containing `end` for any agg its hourly rollup serves (Sum/Avg/Min/Max/Count), independent of which table it actually reads. CNPG's new half-open raw-downsample bound only widened when routing to its own hourly CAGG (Avg/Min/Max only), so a `Sum` query at bucket:1h dropped a sample landing exactly on the window's edge that StarRocks still counted — previously masked by the old inclusive `<=` bound. Fix: in rust/srql/src/query/downsample/sql.rs, added a `hour_grained` condition (whole-hour-multiple bucket, CAGG-safe shape, non-rate agg) that applies the same `time_bucket(...)`/`+ INTERVAL '1 hour'` widened bound used by CNPG's CAGG path even when the raw table is read, matching StarRocks. Added a regression unit test in rust/srql/src/query/tests/translation.rs asserting the widened bound is emitted for a Sum+1h-bucket query. BazelCI: the failing targets (elixir integration_tests_serial_0/3/4/5/6, srql_comprehensive_test) failed with DB-connection-pool exhaustion against the shared fixture Postgres ("too many clients already", DBConnection queue_timeout) — not assertion failures — and this PR touches no Elixir code. This looks like shared-fixture contention/infra flakiness unrelated to the diff; no code change made for it. Did not run cargo/bazel locally per the user's explicit constraint; verification relies on the coordinating session's SrqlParity dispatch on the pushed head

Root cause: User.email is :ci_string, so loaded users carry %Ash.CiString{}, but every email-extracting format_actor clause in record_role_change.ex guarded on is_binary(email). The guard rejected CiString, fell through to the %User{id: id} clause, and the audit row recorded the UUID instead of the email. Also fixed the test assertion to to_string(admin.email) because metadata round-trips through JSONB as plain strings and can never == a CiString struct. Passes (4 tests, OK) after the edit. - Ran on RBE after symlinking the gitignored `.bazelrc.remote` from the primary clone per the hard rule: `bazel test -c opt --config=remote //helm/serviceradar:all //:schema_baseline_freshness_test --test_tag_filters=-integration_test,-acceptance_test` -> 7/7 pass, including `migrations_expected_version_test` and `schema_baseline_freshness_test`. - Grepped the tree for any other reference to `20260904000100`; none outside the migration file itself, so no other pinned copy is stale. no-mistakes(ci): Root cause: migration 20261018140100_backfill_vulnerability_advisory_ordinals.exs ran a synchronous `UPDATE platform.vulnerability_advisories` backfill of about 387k rows on the first-boot path. scripts/db/check-migration-startup-safety.sh rejects that in any migration newer than the baseline. The invariant is that no post-baseline migration does unbounded data maintenance at startup. That work now runs in an idempotent post-bootstrap Oban job, and the allow marker was not added. Changes: - Deleted the 20261018140100 backfill migration. Reverted helm `core.migrations.expectedVersion` to 20261018140000. - Migration 20261018140000 still does only metadata changes: the sequence, a nullable `ordinal` column, and a default for new rows. It also inserts one `maintenance` queue job for the new worker into `platform.oban_jobs`. This copies the existing pattern in 20260926140000_create_otel_service_catalog / OtelServiceCatalogBackfillWorker; the moduledoc explains why the job is enqueued from the migration and not a boot scheduler. - New `ServiceRadar.Inventory.AdvisoryFeeds.OrdinalBackfillWorker` (queue `:maintenance`, unique `period: :infinity, states: :incomplete`, max_attempts 10). In order, it: - numbers rows in 5,000-row transactions, keyset by id, touching only rows `WHERE ordinal IS NULL`, so a retry resumes and never renumbers; - drops any invalid leftover index, then runs `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS`; - sets NOT NULL in steps: an idempotent NOT VALID check, VALIDATE, SET NOT NULL, then drops the check. It logs progress per batch and on completion. Each statement has a 600s timeout. - Loader comments now refer to the job, not the migration. Loader behaviour is unchanged, since it already handles NULL ordinals. - New integration test `test/integration/advisory_ordinal_backfill_worker_integration_test.exs` (unboxed, because CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run in a transaction). It sets up an interrupted state: one of three NULL rows already numbered, plus a leftover NOT VALID check. It then asserts: - all three rows end with distinct ordinals and the pre-numbered row keeps its value; - Postgres catalogs show the column NOT NULL, a valid unique index, and no check constraint; - a second run changes nothing. `on_exit` deletes its rows and puts the column back to its post-migration state. Added the matching entries to INTEGRATION_SOURCE_DISPOSITIONS.tsv and build/integration_test_dispositions.bzl. - Updated the OpenSpec proposal and tasks (1.1, new 1.7 and 2.7), and added a spec scenario for rows the post-startup backfill has not reached yet. Verification (all pass): - scripts/db/check-baseline-metadata.sh and check-migration-startup-safety.sh; - `bazel test //helm/serviceradar:migrations_expected_version_test`; - `bazel test --config=remote` of `//elixir/serviceradar_core:unit_tests_serviceradar_inventory` and `:quality_check`; - the ci_heavy_gate_contract_test suite (57 tests); - `mix credo --strict` on the changed files, with no issues. A local test compile showed warnings only in unrelated files, none in changed files. Not run: the DB integration tests, including the new worker test. They need the srql-fixtures database, which is not available here (no local DB), so BazelCI's integration lanes must run them. Separately, `openspec validate --strict` reports an error that this round did not cause: the MODIFIED Ubuntu requirement replaces the scenario "Unchanged source object is presence only" with a renamed one, and it was left as is. Rollback note: `down` drops the column and does not delete an already-queued job, because a `DELETE FROM platform.oban_jobs` would itself trip the safety check

The failing test was `ServiceRadar.Credentials.CredentialRotationDbTest` "default rotation path refreshes authority and descriptor...", at its `assert "start_rotation" in actions` line. I got this from the child bazel-test invocation's `test.log` through the BuildBuddy API, since the gate's own log retrieval was empty. Cause: this PR routes credential lifecycle events through `OcsfEventPublisher`. Those events are published from inside the rotation action's transaction, so `DurablePublish` only queues them as an outbox job on the `:events` Oban queue. The test then read `platform.ocsf_events` without delivering the outbox, so it found no rows (`actions == []`). That is the intended semantics, and `credential_broker_grant_lifecycle_integration_test.exs` already handles it the same way. Fix: in `elixir/serviceradar_core/test/serviceradar/credentials/credential_rotation_db_test.exs`, I added `Oban.drain_queue(queue: :events)` before the `ocsf_events` query. RustSec audit is external to this PR; no code change warranted. **BazelCI — PR-caused, fixed (1 line).** Different root cause than last round (the harness.rs fix worked; Clippy now passes). The inventory was not updated. Fix: one line adding `"test/phoenix/live/dashboard_live/netflow_map_geo_test.exs"` to `SHARED_FIXTURE_SOURCES` (web_ng_db_runner_contract_test.py:22), at the same alphabetical position the BUILD list uses. I kept the duplication rather than deleting the `srcs` assertion: the target is `size = "enormous"` on shard `serial_0` with a 600s ownership timeout and pool size 8, so the two-key gate makes adding a test to the serial DB lane a conscious act — a deliberate guard, not accidental duplication. Only two files carry this inventory (verified by grep); the other is the BUILD file the PR already updated. Verified locally: - Full CI test phase reproduced: `bazel test -c opt --config=remote --//build:enable_integration_tests //... --test_tag_filters=-integration_test,-acceptance_test,-benchmark` → **260 pass, 2 skipped, 0 failures** across all 262 targets (invocation 2b2a4e94). - `bazel test --nocache_test_results //:web_ng_db_runner_contract_test` → PASSED. - Fail-before proof: deleting the added line reproduces the exact CI assertion (`FAILED in 2 out of 2`); restored after. - `//:all //build:all` → 12/12 pass; `python3 -m unittest ci_heavy_gate_contract_test` → 56 OK (covers the 12 new serviceradar_core tests' TSV dispositions). - Inventory integrity: 28 → 29 unique entries, no duplicates, matching the target's 29 `srcs`. Other new web-ng tests need no registration — `unit_tests` selects via `glob(["test/**/*_test.exs"])`. **RustSec audit — external, no code change.** RUSTSEC-2026-0286 (OOB read decoding CKA_ALLOWED_MECHANISMS) against cryptoki 0.12.0, reached via probe → `ironrdp-connector =0.10.0` → `sspi 0.21.1` → `cryptoki 0.12.0`. Evidence it is not PR-caused: - The job does `cd rust/rdp-connector-probe` and audits only that directory's own lockfile. Base commit `e2827cf9` passed this exact job on staging at 2026-09-16T15:25 (`gh run list`), before it entered the DB. The job `git clone`s advisory-db each run, so staging fails today too. Both remedies are out of scope and a dependency-posture call for the probe's owner: the probe exact-pins the IronRDP family, and the workflow already documents two accepted advisories in this same forced sspi/scard subtree (RUSTSEC-2023-0071, RUSTSEC-2023-0089). cryptoki is PKCS#11 smart-card machinery — the unreachable scard baggage that note covers. no-mistakes(ci): BazelCI failed on one test: `agent_stale_armis_holder` in `//elixir/serviceradar_core:integration_tests_serial_4` (243 tests, 1 failure). I found it by pulling the shard's test.log from BuildBuddy. The failure was a golden mismatch: `Trace_agent_stale_armis_holder.tla` differed from the recorded trace. Cause: the DireTrace harness stamps every Armis sync 60 seconds ahead of now. Before this PR, a new agent check-in released a holder's address without any recency check. The PR added the rule that a no-agent holder releases the address only when the check-in is the newer observation, as the intent requires. In this scenario the "stale" Armis holder was stamped in the future, so the check-in was not newer. The holder correctly kept the address, the recorded trace changed, and the golden no longer matched. The production code is right and the golden file is unchanged. no-mistakes(ci): Fixed the interrupted-ExUnit false-success defect that made the 'Topology validation' (LargeIngestionGate) check report a pass for a run that never completed. Invariant violated: an ExUnit run interrupted by SIGTERM before it prints a suite summary must exit nonzero; the BEAM's default SIGTERM handler shuts down gracefully with exit 0, which the Bazel wrapper records as PASSED. System.at_exit cannot close this hole because signals bypass it, so the fix traps the signal and halts nonzero. Changes (same small correction at the reported site and every sibling full-suite runner helper in serviceradar_core): - elixir/serviceradar_core/test/test_helper.exs (primary; shared by unit, integration, and the large_ingestion_release_gate that owns Topology validation) - elixir/serviceradar_core/test/db/world_worker_fixture_helper.exs - elixir/serviceradar_core/test/cluster_test_helper.exs - elixir/serviceradar_core/bench/bench_test_helper.exs Each registers `System.trap_signal(:sigterm, fn -> IO.puts(:stderr, ...); System.halt(1) end)` with `{:error, :not_sup}` tolerated (RBE is Linux, where trapping is supported). Behavioral subprocess regression (no source-text assertions): new test/serviceradar/exunit_interruption_guard_test.exs spawns a real child `elixir` BEAM loading the real test/test_helper.exs, and asserts observable exit codes — a SIGTERM-interrupted slow suite exits nonzero (guard fires), a passing suite exits 0, and a failing suite exits nonzero. Registered via a `load_only`/`not_selected` row in test/INTEGRATION_SOURCE_DISPOSITIONS.tsv and auto-included through ALL_TEST_SRCS; no serial-count changes apply. Verification run: - Focused remote RBE test `bazel test --config=remote //elixir/serviceradar_core:unit_tests_serviceradar_other` PASSED (invocation fcaf66e8-110c-4441-a55b-a0430d964191). The test log confirms the new file is in the runner's `-r` list and the shard ended '1087 tests, 0 failures, 1 skipped (507 excluded)', so the three new cases executed and the real guard worked on RBE. - build/contracts/ci_heavy_gate_contract_test.py: 56/56 pass (including the disposition-inventory exhaustiveness test that validates the new tsv row). - All five touched .exs files pass Code.string_to_quoted!; git diff --check clean. Invariant violated: a post-promotion assertion must assert only the contract owned by the source type — direct assignments are rewritten by the rollout, but profile members converge via the profile reconciler, so the rollout's contract for a profile source is the moved profile, promoted targets, and cleared overrides (exactly what assert_source_finished checks). The test asserted every latest target's assignment row equals the replacement package, but the fixture hand-builds profile assignments with colon source_keys ("profile_id:uid") while the production reconciler keys rows by hash, so promotion-time reconcile creates new hash-keyed rows on the replacement instead of updating the targets' colon-keyed rows in place, leaving the asserted rows on the old package. Sibling sites enumerated: the pre-promotion profile/assignment package asserts are already correctly per-source scoped (hold); assert_source_finished and the running/staged/privilege guard tests assert only the owned contract (hold); the final loop was the single over-strict site. Fix (test-only, no production change): the per-assignment package assert is now scoped to :assignment sources; the :profile branch instead asserts all member rows (targets' rows plus every profile_assignments row, covering both key representations) carry no rollout override. Re-traced: latest completes, profile moves to replacement, targets promote, colon-row overrides clear via clear_all_overrides, hash rows never hold overrides — all asserts hold for both variants; assignment path behavior unchanged. git diff --check passes. RustSec audit is external to this PR; no code change warranted. **BazelCI — PR-caused, fixed.** Invocation 029d7add: build passed; the integration wave failed exactly one of 12 targets, `//elixir/serviceradar_core:integration_tests_async` (886 tests, 1 failure). Pulled child invocation f86e5447's log from the BuildBuddy API; the single failure is `ServiceRadar.ColdTier.RegistryDriftTest`: ``` ocsf_network_activity: columns exist in the database but not in the cold schema registry (update ServiceRadar.ColdTier.Registry in the same change as the migration): ["flow_uid"] ``` Root cause: this PR added `priv/repo/migrations/20260919120000_add_flow_uid_dedup_key.exs`, which runs `ALTER TABLE platform.ocsf_network_activity ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS flow_uid text`, without updating that table's entry in `ServiceRadar.ColdTier.Registry` — the source of truth for the cold-tier export projection, whose moduledoc requires migrations altering a registry table to update the entry in the same change, enforced by this very test. Two earlier columns (`source_ip`, `src_prefix_tags`) carry comments recording the same omission caught before. Fix: one column tuple appended at elixir/serviceradar_core/lib/serviceradar/cold_tier/registry.ex:321 — `{"flow_uid", "text", :none}` — where the earlier late-added groups sit, with a 3-line comment naming the migration. `text` maps to udt `text` and exports as-is, hence `:none`. Deliberately NOT a tiebreaker: the migration's unique index is partial on `flow_uid IS NOT NULL`, so pre-migration rows carry no identity. Blast radius checked, not assumed: `Verification.checksum_columns/1` has a hard-coded clause for this table (verification.ex:32), so the appended column cannot shift the checksum projection `verification_test.exs` asserts exactly; web-ng's `StorageUsage` uses only `table_names/0` and `schema/0`, never columns; of the four new migrations on this branch only this one alters a registry table, and `ocsf_network_activity` is the registry's last entry, so the aborting assert masked no later drift. Verified against a real database — scratch DB on the srql-fixtures CNPG cluster per the `srql-fixtures-db-tests` skill, all migrations replayed on an empty database (exit 0, `flow_uid` confirmed added): - Fail-before: with the line removed the test reproduced the CI assertion verbatim — 13 tests, 1 failure. - Pass-after: 13 tests, 0 failures; whole `test/serviceradar/cold_tier/` directory 22 tests, 0 failures. - `bazel test -c opt --config=remote //elixir/serviceradar_core:all --test_tag_filters=-integration_test,-acceptance_test,-benchmark` → 18/18 pass (dac8a970). `unit_tests_serviceradar_other` was FLAKY (passed on retry); its failures are `OtelLogsExporterTest`/`AdmissionLaneTest` timing cases, unrelated. - `mix compile` and `mix format --check-formatted` clean. Scratch DB dropped, temp credentials removed. **RustSec audit — external, no code change.** RUSTSEC-2026-0286 against cryptoki 0.12.0, reached only via `rust/rdp-connector-probe` → `ironrdp-connector =0.10.0` → `sspi 0.21.1`. The job audits only that detached crate's own lockfile; its tree hash is byte-identical at base and head (`dceeb5139edc7178c533ba12f1b8e5bf017eac9d`), and `MODULE.bazel`/`rust/rdp-adapter/` are untouched. The audit's entire input is unchanged — the only variable is the advisory DB re-cloned each run. The advisory is dated 2026-09-16; staging's last rust-checks run was 2026-09-16T15:25 on base commit e2827cf9 and succeeded, before the advisory entered the DB, so staging fails today too. Both remedies are out of scope and a dependency-posture call for the probe's owner. The workflow already documents two accepted advisories in this same forced sspi/scard subtree (RUSTSEC-2023-0071, RUSTSEC-2023-0089) — cryptoki is the PKCS#11 smart-card machinery that note covers. no-mistakes(ci): I fixed the test teardown defect and changed one test file only. The fix has not run yet: the DB test executes only in the in-cluster CI lane `topology_atlas_db_test_0`. **Cause:** the `rejoin/2` helper added in the previous round called `leave(socket)` while the old channel was still linked to the test process. In Phoenix 1.8.15, leaving a linked channel exits it with `{:shutdown, :left}`. That exit killed the test at line 318 with `** (EXIT ...) shutdown: :left`. Phoenix's ChannelTest docs say to call `Process.unlink(socket.channel_pid)` first. **Fix:** in `elixir/web-ng/test/phoenix/topology/bitmap_queries_db_test.exs`, `rejoin/2` now does four things in order: - Unlinks the old channel. - Monitors it. - Leaves and asserts the `:ok` reply. - Asserts `{:DOWN, ^monitor, :process, _pid, {:shutdown, :left}}`. That is the actual exit reason from the failing CI run, so the old channel is confirmed gone before the fresh one joins. The unlink applies only to this intentional teardown. Each newly joined channel stays linked, so unexpected crashes still fail the test. Nothing traps or ignores exits. `rejoin/2` was the only place in the test that leaves a linked channel. The final periodic-close check (monitor, then `:normal` after the forbidden `topology_error`) closes the channel through its own refresh and was already handled correctly. **Unchanged:** fresh-channel isolation for the three held-watch cases, the direct DB revocation write, the exact delivery reasons (`query_timeout`, `source_changed`, `forbidden`), the checks that no frame is pushed, the HTTP 403 check, the explicit tick-closure assertion, all production code and deadlines, and all earlier commits. **Verification:** the remote format and Credo check `//elixir/web-ng:quality_check` passed on RBE (https://carverauto.buildbuddy.io/invocation/b896f612-9b82-4885-bfd1-e95708c6e583). The DB test itself was not compiled or run locally

no-mistakes(ci): Fixed the "Native add-on version bumps" check — PR-caused, 1 line. **Root cause.** The previous fix round's RustSec remedy ran `cargo update -p cryptoki --precise 0.12.1`, changing `rust/rdp-connector-probe/Cargo.lock`. That path is explicitly mapped to the `rdp` add-on payload by `scripts/check-native-addon-version-bumps.sh:355-361`, with a comment stating the reason: the RDP helper resolves its connector/CredSSP graph from the isolated `rdp_connector_crates` universe, whose manifest and lockfile live in the probe directory. This is real, not a bookkeeping artifact — `rust/rdp-adapter/BUILD.bazel:8-20` links 13 crates from `@rdp_connector_crates` into the shipped binary, and last round's own verification confirmed the hub re-resolved (`@rdp_connector_crates//:cryptoki-0.12.1`). A re-resolved universe can change the shipped add-on bytes, so the gate requires the manifest version to advance. It did not. **Fix.** `addons/rdp-adapter/addon.yaml:9` — `version: 0.1.7` → `0.1.8`. Nothing else needed updating: `rdp` has no `bazel_version_constant` (only netprobe does), the script's own note at lines 117-131 records that the Rust crate `[package] version` is deliberately decoupled from the manifest, `MODULE.bazel.lock` already recorded the extension's hashes from last round, and the only other `0.1.7` in the repo is an unrelated JS package in `elixir/web-ng/assets/pnpm-lock.yaml`. I deliberately did NOT touch the gate. AGENTS.md states that teaching it to skip a path trades a false positive for a false negative — a changed artifact shipping under an unchanged version — which is the gate's entire purpose. **Verification (every claim has a command behind it):** - Fail-before control, the gate's exact CI invocation against the same base commit: `scripts/check-native-addon-version-bumps.sh e2827cf9 HEAD` → exit 1, reproducing the CI message verbatim: `error: rdp native add-on payload changed but addons/rdp-adapter/addon.yaml stayed at 0.1.7`. - Pass-after, same command against a temp commit-tree carrying the bump → `native add-on version bump check passed`, exit 0. - `bazel test -c opt --config=remote --nocache_test_results //build/native_addons:build_gates_test` → **10/10 tests pass** (invocation ebc2d84d), including `validate_addon_manifests_test`, `inventory_consistency_test` and `//scripts:native_addon_version_bumps_test` (the gate script's own unit tests). The build re-ran the `rdp_adapter_addon_bundle` genrule successfully, so the edited manifest still assembles into the signed bundle. Final diff: 1 file, 1 line

no-mistakes(ci): This was a scheduling bug in the workflow, not a product failure: the existing network and plugin DB cases ran before the scale test and used up its reserved time. The fix runs the scale test first and gives the existing cases whatever time is left; no limits changed. Changes are uncommitted. **Root cause.** In compact scale mode, `buildbuddy.yaml` (WebNgDbDiagnostic) ran `networks_live_db_test` (378–406s in hosted CI) and `plugin_config_cli_db_test` before checking whether the scale test could still fit. In run 8e2780c9 the 2,925s admission check came 435s after the observer started, leaving only 2,865s of observer time, so scale was refused without seeding. The invariant: every scale-mode phase must start only if both the action deadline and the observer deadline still cover it plus the 165s reserve (30s quiet wait, two 60s cleanup commands, 5s kill grace, 10s status), and any case that runs out of time must fail the run. **Change (`buildbuddy.yaml`).** - New order: provision `serial_0`, plus `serial_1` for sparse, as before. Then admit and run the scale test. Then run the network case, then the plugin case. Both existing cases still run and are still required. - Compact seeds `serial_0` and its existing cleanup deletes its rows, test user and ordinal sequence position before the other cases use that database. Sparse uses `serial_1`. - A new `scale_remaining` function holds the shared deadline arithmetic. `admit_scale` keeps the same 2,925s floor and refusal message. - A new `limit_ordinary_suite` runs before each existing case in scale mode. It re-reads both clocks and wraps the case in `timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=5s` using whatever is left beyond the 165s reserve. If nothing is left it prints "Diagnostic budget exhausted after scale …" and fails the run, starting nothing further. - Ordinary (non-scale) runs are unchanged: no timeout wrapper, same order and behavior. - All limits are unchanged: 3300s observer, 3600s outer, 2700s Bazel test / 2640s ExUnit, 2755s scale envelope, 2925s floor, 120s cleanup, 30s quiet wait, plus the pool slots, workload and native caps. **Limitation.** The phases cannot all use their maximum time in one run. If the scale test uses its full 2,755s, about 325s remain — less than a hosted network run has taken — so that run fails instead of passing. This is now documented. **Tests (`build/contracts/ci_heavy_gate_contract_test.py`).** - The existing executable shell harness now has a clock the fake Bazel calls advance. - Order and timeout checks: in scale mode the order is scale, network, plugin, each existing case gets a timeout (3080s with the default clocks), and the observer settings are unchanged. - Budget cases: - scale 2000s, network 400s: timeouts of 1080s then 680s, both cases run. - scale 2755s: both cases get 325s. - scale 2755s, network 400s: the plugin case is refused and the run fails. - scale 3082s: neither case starts and the run fails. - Existing admission-boundary, observer-limit, bad-clone and cleanup tests are preserved. **Docs.** `docs/topology-bitmap-scale-acceptance.md` now describes the new order, the per-case budget, compact's cleanup on `serial_0`, and the limitation above. The scale-acceptance entry in the OpenSpec `choices.md` is updated to match. The proposal, design, spec and tasks don't describe this order, so they need no change, and `choices.md` is not one of the portable review's checksummed sources. **Verification (all `--config=remote`).** - `//build/contracts:ci_heavy_gate_contract_test` passed (bf9bc97c-16b3-45a5-b7df-2f14b4535630; rerun cached pass 44cdb7bc-8200-4f76-b542-634901636e69). - Moving the scale block back after the existing cases turned 6 subtests red (59 tests run); the file was then restored. - `git diff --check` is clean. **Not run.** Hosted WebNgDbDiagnostic compact and sparse; they need publication and dispatch on the new SHA. Tasks 4.2 and 4.7 stay open, and there are still no scale measurements

no-mistakes(ci): Fixed the sparse WebNgDbDiagnostic failure: the hinted replica refused 23,286 hints at its 3,670,016-byte retained-memory bound during ticks 60 and 66-70. Invariant: when hint resolution is cheap, a slow publication or scan step must not leave UIDs piled up behind it until they hit the retained-memory bound. Scan and catalog service must still get a finite, fixed share of turns. Root cause, from the evidence files: resolving a batch of 500 UIDs costs about 8 ms (11,437 ms over 1,439 batches). Dirty publication costs about 89 ms when stable and 196-251 ms under contention, and a scan page costs 174-227 ms. The old rotation was hints, dirty, hints, dirty, scan, catalog, with a 25-ms pause after every success. That allowed only 2 cheap resolutions per expensive cycle (about 1,300 UIDs/s under contention against 2,200/s arriving). Meanwhile the waiting UIDs held the BitmapHints budget. The native Roaring dirty set has its own 512-KiB serialized bound and asks for a rescan on overflow, so a publication backlog belongs there, not in the UID queue. Change (`elixir/web-ng/lib/serviceradar_web_ng/topology/bitmap_index.ex`), two small edits: 1. The rotation is now hints, dirty, hints, dirty, hints, scan, hints, catalog. Each cycle gets 4 resolutions, 2 publications of 500 rows, 1 scan page and the catalog. Scan/catalog keep a fixed one-in-eight turn, and missing work is still skipped, so a cold replica without hints scans at the same rate. 2. After a successful step, the next one starts with no pause while BitmapHints still holds UIDs. Otherwise the 25-ms pause applies as before. Estimate under the measured contention: about 2,900 resolved UIDs/s, enough for the 2,200/s arriving. Unchanged: one worker, 500-row batches, the 3.5-MiB/512-KiB limits, native budgets, retries/backoff/timeouts and failure semantics. No new publishers, caches, outbox or leases. Docs: `docs/topology-bitmap-scale-acceptance.md` now records the first compact and sparse results at 183be181f4. Compact is recorded with its limitation: one 5,155-ms tick, so not every tick stayed under 5 s. The file also describes the new scheduler and states it is NOT verified until compact and sparse are rerun on the same published SHA. The scheduler paragraph in `openspec/.../design.md` is updated the same way. No new unit test. The scheduler calls the database through BitmapSource and has no production injection seam, and adding a test-only seam would break the test-audit rule. The real behavioral regression is the hosted sparse acceptance, which failed on the old code. It has to be rerun after publication, along with compact. Verification, all via `--config=remote`: - `//elixir/web-ng:quality_check` (format + Credo) passed: 228bcc86-aa74-430a-be5b-f75bdc3948fc. - `//elixir/web-ng:topology_bitmap_scale_harness_test` passed: e960b8f0-1c54-4403-8dcb-91a0b1400637. The command itself exited with a pattern-parse error because I first gave a wrong `:quality` target name, then I ran `quality_check` on its own. - `openspec validate --strict` passed and `git diff --check` is clean. Not run: the full `make test`, the hosted DB lifecycle, and the compact/sparse scale workloads. Those need publication. I made no commit. If you commit locally, use `SERVICERADAR_SKIP_ELIXIR_FORMAT=1`, since formatting was already checked remotely

no-mistakes(ci): Fixed 2 of 3 failing checks; the third is external to this PR. **BazelCI + Clippy (PR-caused, fixed):** Both failed on one root cause. This PR added the `starrocks_database` field to `srql::config::AppConfig` (rust/srql/src/config.rs:16) and updated the three in-crate test constructors (server.rs:311, query/tests.rs:68, query/starrocks.rs:965), but missed the out-of-crate constructor in the SRQL integration harness. BuildBuddy invocation 38f7e8fb shows `error[E0063]: missing field starrocks_database in initializer of AppConfig` at harness.rs:106 three times (//integration_tests/srql:srql_api_test, :srql_comprehensive_test, :srql_device_grouped_stats_test) and no other error; Clippy hit the identical error on srql-integration-tests. Fix: one line in integration_tests/srql/tests/support/harness.rs:110 adding `starrocks_database: "serviceradar".to_string(),`, matching the literal the three sibling test configs already use. No other AppConfig literal in the repo was missing the field (verified by grep). Verified locally: `bazel build -c opt --config=remote --//build:enable_integration_tests` on all three previously-failing targets -> exit 0; `cargo clippy -p srql-integration-tests --all-targets -- -D warnings` -> exit 0. **RustSec audit (external, no code change):** RUSTSEC-2026-0286 against cryptoki 0.12.0, a transitive dep (sspi -> cryptoki) of rust/rdp-connector-probe, the detached review-only IronRDP probe. Evidence it is not PR-caused: `git diff e2827cf9..682c1f8a -- rust/rdp-connector-probe/` is empty (audited Cargo.lock byte-identical to base); the advisory was assigned upstream 2026-09-17T07:37:14Z; the base commit e2827cf9 passed this same audit on staging at 2026-09-16T15:25, before the advisory existed; the job clones a fresh advisory-db each run, so staging fails it today too. The two possible remedies both exceed scope: bumping cryptoki would alter a detached crate's dependency tree unrelated to StarRocks analytics, and `--ignore RUSTSEC-2026-0286` would suppress a live vulnerability -- a dependency-posture call for the probe's owner, alongside the two advisories already accepted there with written justifications. Note: //integration_tests/srql targets compile only under `--//build:enable_integration_tests`, so `make test` and a plain local `bazel build //...` would not catch this class of break -- the pre-existing comment in buildbuddy.yaml documents the same failure mode from a prior incident

This is exposed because the PR touches `elixir/serviceradar_core_elx/**`, which makes the workflow run that leg. Verified locally: `mix deps.get --check-locked` exits 0 in core_elx; `./scripts/elixir_quality.sh --project elixir/serviceradar_core_elx --lint-only` exits 0 (mix format + credo --strict clean); `bazel test //third_party/hex:gen_test` PASSED. No other project's lock is affected (`serviceradar_core`'s lock check already passes, and the other legs were green in the failing run). no-mistakes(ci): BazelCI failed in `//elixir/serviceradar_core:integration_tests_serial_5`. All 6 `DireResolutionTraceTest` cases failed with `File.Error: could not read file "/buildbuddy-execroot/.mix_erlang_app_serviceradar_core/formal/dire/traces/Trace_<name>.tla": no such file or directory`. I got this from the child invocation's `test.log`, since the outer log was only a tail. Cause: `ServiceRadar.DireTrace` fixed its trace directory at compile time with `Path.expand("../../../../formal/dire/traces", __DIR__)`. That works under plain `mix`. Under Bazel, mix_app compiles in its own build tree, so the baked path points at a directory that doesn't exist in the test sandbox. The traces are already declared data (`//formal/dire:traces` via `INTEGRATION_RUNTIME_DATA`) and sit two levels above the test's cwd, `elixir/serviceradar_core`. Fix, in `elixir/serviceradar_core/test/support/dire_trace.ex`: `golden!/3` now resolves the directory at runtime through a new `traces_dir/0`. It uses the compile-time path if that directory exists, otherwise `../../formal/dire/traces` relative to the cwd. This follows the `repo_root/0` pattern in `addon_config_contract_fixtures.ex` and `plugins_root/0` in `credential_integration_fixtures.ex`. `DIRE_TRACE_WRITE=1` under plain `mix` still writes to the same place, and the trace content and comparison are unchanged. Verification: I could only confirm the file parses (`Code.string_to_quoted!`), because `mix compile` and `mix format` can't run here without fetched deps. The DB-backed test can't run here either, so the real check is the next BazelCI run

Under plain `go test` all *_test.go files compile together so this works, but Bazel only sees the declared srcs and fails with an undefined symbol. Fix: Added a self-contained newGRPCTestCAAndLeaf helper directly in plugin_runtime_grpc_test.go (using crypto/ecdsa, crypto/x509, a synthetic 192.0.2.10 IP SAN, and distinct names to avoid collision with the existing helper). Updated the single call site to use the new name. Added the required imports (crypto/ecdsa, crypto/elliptic, crypto/rand, crypto/x509/pkix, encoding/pem, math/big). Verified: go vet passes, test binary compiles (go test -c), and all TestPluginHostGRPCUnary* tests pass (exit 0)

no-mistakes(ci): BazelCI failed on //elixir/serviceradar_core:integration_tests_async with 2 failures, both in this PR's new test ('a newer approved candidate replaces a failed paused assignment/profile rollout...'): after prior-version recovery reports, targets stayed :rollback_pending instead of reaching :rolled_back. Invariant violated: a rollback-recovery status evaluated by evaluate_rollback_target (which gates on supervision_ready?/2 = state-ready AND non-degraded) must carry no degradation reason left over from the earlier failure report sharing its {agent_uid, addon_id} upsert identity. The failure loop wrote degradation_reason 'test_failure' via report_status/6, but the recovery loop used report_status_for/5, which omits that field, so the Ash upsert preserved the stale failure reason, degraded?/1 stayed true, and the targets never transitioned. Sibling sites enumerated: the recovery loop is the single site needing the fix (it covers both :assignment and :profile via the for-source_type loop); the failure loop intentionally sets degradation (correct); replacement-health reports and convergence probes are evaluated by candidate_ready?/version_at_least (ignore degradation, unaffected). Fix: recovery loop now uses report_status/6 with 'running'/true, which explicitly rewrites degradation_reason to nil — matching every existing rollback-recovery test. Re-traced: recovery advance now yields :rolled_back, supersede_failed_candidate leaves :rolled_back targets untouched (mark_targets_canceled skips them), satisfying the later Enum.all? assertion; no production code or shared helpers touched. git diff --check passes. No local build/test run: user intent forbids local Mix/Bazel/DB work for this step — PR BazelCI is the verifier

no-mistakes(ci): Root cause found via BuildBuddy full CI log (bb view): test/serviceradar/repo/ash_schema_migrations_sync_db_test.exs "under web-ng's config, the task leaves core's ledger complete" drops platform.schema_migrations and assumes platform.ash_schema_migrations already holds the full migration history. That assumption only holds when a developer ran mix serviceradar.db.migrate locally first; the shared BazelCI/CNPG scratch fixture (sr_core_template) never populates the ash ledger unless something was pending, so ash_schema_migrations was empty/missing in this run. With both ledgers effectively empty but 414 real platform objects present, SchemaBootstrap.classify/1 correctly returned {:ambiguous, ...} and MigrateTask.run/1 raised "ambiguous database state" instead of :ok — exactly what CI showed. This is a test defect (an unguaranteed environment assumption), not a bug in sync_migration_ledgers!/1 or the migrate task. Fixed by seeding the ash ledger explicitly with every on-disk migration version before dropping the core ledger, mirroring the pattern already used by sibling tests via lag_ledger!/1. Extracted the shared seeding logic (create-table-if-missing + insert all on-disk versions) out of lag_ledger!/1 into a new seed_ledger!/1 helper used by both. No production code changed. Did not run the BazelCI/DB-backed suite locally (per this workspace's rule against cold-compiling serviceradar_core or hitting the shared srql-fixtures CNPG from this step); verified the logic by tracing classify/1, sync_migration_ledgers!/1, and MigrateTask.run/1 against the corrected test setup

no-mistakes(ci): Fixed the shared test-only timing probe in audit_events_live_test.exs (sole file changed; no production, assertion, timeout, lane, or pin changes). Invariants: (1) receive-offset measurements must use source event timestamps, not collector scheduling time — enabled ERTS :monotonic_timestamp and converted trace_ts nanosecond stamps to ms offsets from send-start, handling all trace_ts/trace shapes with no global patterns. (2) A reported latency window must exclude instrumentation setup — send_start_ns is now established after telemetry.attach/tracer spawn with separate send/assert windows logged (window_ms, assert_window_ms). (3) A post-assertion diagnostic snapshot must be coherent and never conflate unobserved with absent — telemetry still sends :audit_read first (order preserved), the handler stamps query completion at the source, and the after-block collects within a bounded 150ms grace after the already-decided 1000ms assert (no window extension/retry/rescue), capturing query_completed_ms instead of discarding it and reporting -1 as unobserved. (4) Cleanup must never raise on a dead target or leak tracing — both after-block and on_exit paths use a guarded disable (alive check + ArgumentError rescue, clearing exactly the owned :receive+:monotonic_timestamp flags on view.pid only) with independent tracer stop.
